question: How much revenue do missed calls cost Punctual Pros?
html:
What missed calls cost Punctual Pros

Missed calls cost Punctual Pros about $1.4M a year in recoverable revenue (est.) under a conservative model: about $390k after hours and $982k from daytime and storm overflow (Voice AI research). Call volume, missed-call rate and booking rate are all modelled rather than measured, so treat this as a range.

How the estimate is built

  • Inbound calls of about 3,502 a month are backed out of est. revenue of ~$22M. The model assumes 70% of revenue is call-driven at a $1,024 average ticket (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
  • The missed share of 14.8% blends two figures (Voice AI research):
  • 12% of calls arrive after hours, and 35% of those are lost.
  • 88% arrive in the daytime, and 12% of those are missed or abandoned.
  • Haircuts are applied after that. The model assumes AI recovers 80% of missed calls, books 45% of them, and counts only 60% as incremental to allow for callers who would have called back.
InputValue (est.)
Inbound calls per month3,502
Missed share14.8% (range 10-35%)
Incremental jobs per year1,343
Recovered revenue$1,372,000

Why the true figure may differ

  • Revenue base is soft. FY2025 revenue is est. at ~$22M, with a range of $16-28M and medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings). Call volume scales directly with this figure.
  • Missed share could be much higher. Invoca finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (65% for calls over 15 seconds). The model's 14.8% sits near the low end of its 10-35% range (Voice AI research).
  • Losses are seasonal. Off-hours calls are 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October. October is the busiest HVAC month nationally (Punctual Pros demand model). Peak-season leakage is likely above the annual average.
  • Vendor numbers are unaudited. The booking rates come from ServiceTitan (70% overall, 90% with open capacity) and are self-reported (Voice AI research).

Related revenue upside

  • An outbound AI renewal lift adds about $403k a year (est.). That figure assumes 6,000 members, an 8-point renewal gain and $840 of annual value per member.
  • Combined with recovered calls, the total is about $1.775M, or roughly 8.1% of est. revenue (Voice AI research).
  • The membership count is assumed, not known.

What would replace the estimate

Actual data from the ServiceTitan or phone system would replace the modelled inputs:

  • answered versus abandoned calls by hour
  • booking rate by customer service rep
  • calls that went to voicemail but never called back
  • current membership count and renewal rate

Next actions

  1. Pull 12 months of Punctual Pros call logs and ServiceTitan bookings. Use them to replace the modelled call volume, missed share and booking rate.
  2. Split the missed calls by month and by after-hours versus daytime. This tests the June and storm-peak concentration.
  3. Confirm the membership count and renewal rate before sizing the outbound renewal upside.
  4. Scope a time-boxed after-hours AI pilot in one PA territory. Measure incremental booked jobs against a holdout territory.

# What missed calls cost Punctual Pros

Missed calls cost Punctual Pros about **$1.4M a year in recoverable revenue (est.)** under a conservative model: about $390k after hours and $982k from daytime and storm overflow (Voice AI research). Call volume, missed-call rate and booking rate are all modelled rather than measured, so treat this as a range.

## How the estimate is built

- Inbound calls of about 3,502 a month are backed out of est. revenue of ~$22M. The model assumes 70% of revenue is call-driven at a $1,024 average ticket (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
- The missed share of 14.8% blends two figures (Voice AI research):
  - 12% of calls arrive after hours, and 35% of those are lost.
  - 88% arrive in the daytime, and 12% of those are missed or abandoned.
- Haircuts are applied after that. The model assumes AI recovers 80% of missed calls, books 45% of them, and counts only 60% as incremental to allow for callers who would have called back.

| Input | Value (est.) |
|---|---|
| Inbound calls per month | 3,502 |
| Missed share | 14.8% (range 10-35%) |
| Incremental jobs per year | 1,343 |
| Recovered revenue | $1,372,000 |

## Why the true figure may differ

- **Revenue base is soft.** FY2025 revenue is est. at ~$22M, with a range of $16-28M and medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings). Call volume scales directly with this figure.
- **Missed share could be much higher.** Invoca finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (65% for calls over 15 seconds). The model's 14.8% sits near the low end of its 10-35% range (Voice AI research).
- **Losses are seasonal.** Off-hours calls are 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October. October is the busiest HVAC month nationally (Punctual Pros demand model). Peak-season leakage is likely above the annual average.
- **Vendor numbers are unaudited.** The booking rates come from ServiceTitan (70% overall, 90% with open capacity) and are self-reported (Voice AI research).

## Related revenue upside

- An outbound AI renewal lift adds about $403k a year (est.). That figure assumes 6,000 members, an 8-point renewal gain and $840 of annual value per member.
- Combined with recovered calls, the total is about $1.775M, or roughly 8.1% of est. revenue (Voice AI research).
- The membership count is assumed, not known.

## What would replace the estimate

Actual data from the ServiceTitan or phone system would replace the modelled inputs:
- answered versus abandoned calls by hour
- booking rate by customer service rep
- calls that went to voicemail but never called back
- current membership count and renewal rate

## Next actions

1. Pull 12 months of Punctual Pros call logs and ServiceTitan bookings. Use them to replace the modelled call volume, missed share and booking rate.
2. Split the missed calls by month and by after-hours versus daytime. This tests the June and storm-peak concentration.
3. Confirm the membership count and renewal rate before sizing the outbound renewal upside.
4. Scope a time-boxed after-hours AI pilot in one PA territory. Measure incremental booked jobs against a holdout territory.
